uncertainty_method: Arithmetic mirror-pair mean within each block; Student t interval on3 block log ratios(df2). Pointwise intervals; no multiple-comparison adjustment. Every sample retained in primary estimates; leave-one-whole-block-out calculations are sensitivity only.
limitations: Fixed20M startup workload, not steady-state sustained insertion or tail-neutrality evidence.

Each worker owns2.5M fixed records, so workers finish at different times and concurrency falls in the tail. Final operation and deregistration timings do not measure earlier foreground-compaction work.
Processes taskset0-11 allows worker migration and variable SMT placement, unlike controlled-cache individually pinned workers. Four background workers share those CPUs.
Before/after thermal/frequency snapshots are not phase frequency measurements. Only3s excluded preconditions; first-control thermal transients remain visible and all samples are retained.
The earlier5s timed-noWAL loss came mainly from post-sample join tails; this fixed-quota test does not reproduce or resolve the cause of that original timing effect.
Full body/drain CPU uses process CPU clocks and includes foreground and background work. Legacy cpu_us_op is only sampled-window CPU and is not used for headline comparisons.
Exact drain timing is worker_start through after_close, including preclose summary writing; elapsed_s plus rounded close_s omits/rounds those boundaries and is not used here.
Three blocks yield broad intervals; apparent wall-throughput loss cannot be dismissed solely because full-window CPU/op is near equal.
